transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-19
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 68 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Liu (CSM), Diego Ramos (SE) — EmberPoint: Aisha Khan (Head of MLOps), Tom Reynolds (Platform Eng), Priya Desai (Security Lead), Liam O'Connor (Product)

Summary:
Quick immersion kickoff to align on staging -> private deployment ramp, security checkpoints, perf expectations and success metrics for initial pilot. Agreed deliverables: runbook, perf checklist, sample telemetry, security review.

Topics:
- Staging topology and onboarding steps
- Network requirements for VPC/private deployment and KMS/HSM
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs; batching/quantization recommendations
- Pilot success criteria and roll-out timeline

Action items (also listed in metadata): see action_items

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick note — we'll run through the immersion plan, security touch points, and then move into the ops ramp. We're aiming for a pilot in staging first.
[00:18] Aisha (EmberPoint): Yep, thanks. we've got Tom and Priya here, liam too. goal for us is to validate throughput for live inference behind our internal API and confirm the data handling meets our compliance needs.
[00:34] Diego (Redwood SE): cool — curious, Aisha, can you give a quick run-down of your expected qps and payload sizes, and whether you plan on streaming responses or full-output returns?
[00:46] Aisha: We're looking at bursts of 200 qps for short prompts (~30-80 tokens) and smaller long-form generation for support replies (~400-600 tokens) but that's like 5% of traffic. For now non-streaming is fine but we may add streaming later.
[01:05] Tom (EmberPoint): one note: our infra lives in GCP in europe-west1; security will want KMS integration and logs forwarded to our SIEM — that's Priya's area.
[01:20] Priya (EmberPoint): yep. also we need SOC2 style artifact for key rotation and HSM options; don't want keys in plaintext in any third party. are you offering customer-managed keys?
[01:33] Connor (Redwood CSM): yes — Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and we have an onboarding checklist for SAML/Sso and audit logs. we'll share our security pack; maya will drop link in follow up. (note: link placeholder — https://redwood.internal/security/emb-emberpoint)
[01:52] Priya: ok we'll need the SOC2 cert and the compliance matrix please.
[02:00] Maya: absolutely, we'll include SOC 2, ISO references and our data handling whitepaper. quick q on latency SLA — what's your target p95?
[02:12] Liam (EmberPoint): target p95 for short prompts is sub-200ms, but we can accept sub-350ms for the pilot if cost delta is too high. success metric is both latency and error rate <1%.
[02:29] Diego: ok — that helps. our dedicated pools can hit sub-200ms for those prompt sizes on A100 equivalent config with small batching and prefix caching. we can propose a quantized model variant for cost reduction that increases p95 by ~30ms.
[02:46] Tom: that 30ms could matter. do you have measured numbers for quantization on longer sequences? our long responses we tolerate higher p95 but throughput matters.
[03:00] Diego: for 400–600 tokens quantized 4-bit runs showed 10–15% slower per-token but cost drops 40–50%. we can run a short perf-run in your staging with your real prompts to quantify — I'll prepare a notebook and a perf checklist.
[03:20] Aisha: yes please — we'll provide the prompt set. also curious about caching — we have a lot of repeated prefixes in our support flows, kv cache could help.
[03:33] Diego: KV/prefix caching is part of Redwood Optimize; with repeated prefixes we typically see 20–35% token savings depending on cache hit rate. need asked questions about stateful sessions — are you planning to keep full session context server-side?
[03:49] Tom: we store last 5 messages per session in our DB and include them on API calls, so the inference call is stateless from your perspective. we might experiment with session-level caching later.
[04:02] Priya: security question — when you say 'cache', is anything persisted off-prem? we need guarantees for purging and retention controls.
[04:10] Maya: good flag — for Redwood Private all caching can be kept within customer's VPC and lifespan controlled by policy. we'll include the purge API in the runbook.
[04:24] Liam: great. onboarding timeline? capital we have a Q3 launch window but flexible.
[04:30] Connor: suggested timeline — week 0: staging provisioning + network tests; week 1–2: perf runs and security review; week 3: pilot go/no-go; week 4: scale plan. we can compress if you want.
[04:45] Aisha: that aligns. one blocker for us is internal procurement — we need an initial cost estimate and a small pilot commitment number to ingest into budget.
[04:55] Maya: we'll send a high-level cost model after we get your token mix and expected qps — Diego will prepare perf data and a recommended config. note: cost model will include hosted vs dedicated vs private delta.
[05:10] Tom: network rules — will we need to open outbound to any Redwood-managed endpoints for control-plane? we prefer minimal egress.
[05:21] Diego: with Redwood Private, the control plane can be customer-hosted in your VPC; only a heartbeat to the control plane is needed if you want metrics; we can also go air-gapped if required but that adds integration work.
[05:36] Priya: good to know. for pilot we probably want control-plane-in-VPC. can we get a runbook for the control-plane handshake and firewall ports?
[05:44] Maya: yes — runbook will include ports, expected CIDRs, and TLS cert handshake steps. also a pre-checklist for the network team.
[05:58] Diego: quick deep-dive: model variants — we recommend starting with a mid-size open model we have verified in the catalog, then consider 4-bit quantization and an int8 accelerated path on dedicated GPUs. this gives deterministic latency and cost control for the pilot.
[06:18] Aisha: how do rollbacks look if we see quality regressions after quantization?
[06:25] Diego: Redwood supports automatic fallback policies — we can do canary with 10% traffic to the quantized variant and automatic fallback to the backed full-precision model on quality regression thresholds you set. rollouts are managed via the Console.
[06:40] Liam: can we tie quality alerts to our test prompt set? like if perplexity deviates or answer correctness dips?
[06:48] Connor: yes — Redwood Optimize can run evals against your prompt set and trigger alerts; we'll need the exact prompt and expected outputs (or scoring rubric) to configure it.
[07:02] Aisha: we'll prepare that. also wanted to clarify data residency — logs and prompts must remain in our EU region for regulatory reasons.
[07:14] Maya: understood — we'll pin the region to europe-west1 for the pilot and ensure logs and backups stay within region. will include retention policy options.
[07:25] Tom: does the onboarding require an agent or do you provide IaC templates for provisioning?
[07:32] Diego: we provide Terraform modules and a sample CloudFormation — for GCP it's Terraform. we'll share examples and the perf notebook.
[07:43] Priya: encryption in transit and at rest — we need to review how you manage ephemeral keys and KMS integration.
[07:51] Maya: will include KMS architecture diagram, KMS/HSM options, and an explanation of customer-managed keys flow in the security pack.
[07:59] Liam: any competitors we should consider? our infra folks asked about Anthropic enterprise and also building an internal endpoint.
[08:08] Connor: those are common. Redwood differentiators here are production batching, observability at token-level, and rollout controls. we'll send a short competitor comparison doc.
[08:19] Aisha: ok. let's talk pilot success criteria — Luca, actually liam — you mentioned p95 and error rate. Anything else?
[08:28] Liam: reliability (>99.9% uptime during pilot), cost within target budget, and a set of quality checks passing for NLU tasks.
[08:37] Diego: noted. I'll include suggested probes and synthetic tests to validate those metrics. also propose a small smoke test harness that your platform team can run.
[08:48] Tom: for the perf run, what permissions will you need? we prefer not to provide service account keys; can you run with short-lived tokens or a delegated pipeline?
[08:59] Diego: yes — we support ephemeral credentials and can run perf jobs via a CI job you trigger. we'll provide a job template for your CI.
[09:10] Aisha: great. Question: can we preview the Console dashboards to ensure the metrics we care about are surfaced?
[09:17] Connor: yes, we can give a demo tenant this week. Maya will coordinate a 30-minute console walkthrough.
[09:26] Maya: I'll schedule that and include the security pack and cost model in the email.
[09:31] Liam: perfect. Any open concerns from security side, Priya?
[09:35] Priya: just to reiterate: proof of key custody, audit log forwarding, SSO + RBAC mapping, and contractual SLAs. also we want a runbook for incident response with contact rotations.
[09:48] Maya: we'll include an incident response template and contact rotation example in the runbook.
[09:55] Diego: quick note on data deletion — we support API-driven data purge and retention policies; we'll document the endpoint and sample requests.
[10:04] Aisha: awesome. Logistics — do we need a PO up front for pilot or can we start with a credit-backed trial?
[10:11] Connor: typically we do a pilot credit arrangement for tests under $X, and a committed pilot quote for anything larger. we'll review after Diego sees the token mix.
[10:22] Tom: ok that helps procurement.
[10:26] Maya: to recap the next steps — (1) Redwood sends runbook, security docs, Terraform modules, and cost starter model by 2028-07-22; (2) EmberPoint sends prompt set and token distribution by 2028-07-25; (3) Diego will prepare perf notebook and sample CI job by 2028-07-24; (4) schedule Console walkthrough and security deep-dive week of 2028-07-26.
[10:52] Aisha: sounds good. any final questions?
[10:55] Liam: none here. thanks everyone.
[10:57] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with artifacts. I'll tag action items in the CRM. bye.
